title: Early W2 variability predicts later variability in 121 low-offset dust candidates with field kinematics
abstract: We test whether infrared variability persists across separate time windows in the published NEOWISE 2014-2024 dust sample. We use all eligible candidates, not a sample selected by the full time series. We remove a separate constant for each observing season within each window. We rank the W2 residual scatter against 200 controls matched in brightness, error and visit count. In 121 low-offset candidates with field kinematics, 9 of 15 early variables also vary later, against 11 of 106 without an early flag. Brightness and colour-excess strata predict 4.02 joint flags under conditional independence; the data give 9 (one-sided exact p = 0.0006491). Controls also show cross-window dependence. The result supports repeated measurable activity within this candidate group, but does not prove distinct dust-production events. It can reflect a long changing dust state, source-specific noise or a persistent blend. The analysis reuses published visit medians and adds no sky observations. Field kinematics do not measure age.
